survey: A DJ controller made of three sections in a row (left deck, centre mixer, right deck) lies flat on an orange floor, seen from above at roughly 35-40° with one corner towards the viewer. Its edges run in two directions on the page, about 25° and 143°, and its short corner edges stay near vertical. If those two edge directions meet at a right angle on the real object, the camera is about 36° above the floor, which matches the platter ellipses (ratios 0.59-0.65, short axes near vertical). Each centre hub matches its rim (0.59 vs 0.60 on the right, 0.65 vs 0.65 on the left), and the nearer left platter is slightly rounder. Pads, button rows and fader slots run parallel to the deck edges and shrink slightly towards the back. Knobs are upright cylinders with their tops seen from above. A raised display box on the back of the left deck uses the same edge directions. A pair of headphones stands upright on the same floor in front of the right part of the controller, with a contact shadow. One cup shows its cushion and the other its outer shell, which fits cups swivelled flat; their ellipses differ only slightly. Every part reads as one camera and one ground plane.
